accent.description: provenance-derived accent from self-reported demographics (not measured from audio): { origin_country (ISO-3166 childhood country where the accent forms), english_native (true if English is the first language, else false; null if unknown) }

audio_metrics.description: measured from THIS track, at the rate this archive ships. Conformance, DNSMOS, and physical time-series measurements land independently, so one can exist while another is null; the block itself is null only when none exists

dnsmos_bak_median.description: ITU-T P.835 background-noise median on the nominal 1-5 mean-opinion-score scale, 5 = not noticeable; calibrated predictions can fall outside this range

dnsmos_ovr_median.description: ITU-T P.835 overall median, nominal 1-5: voice and background together; calibrated predictions can fall outside this range

dnsmos_sig_median.description: ITU-T P.835 speech-signal median, nominal 1-5: the voice itself; calibrated predictions can fall outside this range

dnsmos_time_series.description: names the file holding the same three scores over time

effective_bandwidth_hz.description: effective bandwidth in Hz. Measurement version 4 uses the 99.99% energy cutoff during detected speech. Null when unmeasured or unmeasurable

noise_floor_dbfs.description: the room in dBFS, lower = quieter. Null where the track has not been measured yet, which is most of the catalogue today; on a measured track, null means there is no room tone to measure at all

signal_metrics_time_series.description: names the file holding SNR, noise floor, and clipping percentage over time

silence_profile.description: what fills this track when the speaker is not talking, measured from the audio rather than from any capture flag. "room_tone" (the actual room), "noise_gated" (the capture chain wrote digital silence between turns), "dropout" (the microphone cut out mid-recording, audio either side), "no_signal" (nothing was ever voiced). Null is unmeasured rather than a fifth shape

silent_while_partner_spoke_pct.description: share of the partner's speech during which this microphone carried no signal, the trailing pad excluded. Read it beside the silence_profile of BOTH tracks: 0 means the overlap survived only where this track is room_tone or noise_gated and the partner voiced something, and a high value means a gate erased that overlap. Two shapes force 0 with no overlap behind it — a no_signal track, whose whole file is the excluded pad, and any track whose PARTNER is no_signal, because the partner's speech is the denominator. A dropout forces neither, because its hole has audio either side of it and is counted. Gated tracks run the whole range, so this is what tells a lightly affected track from a gutted one. Null is unmeasured

avg_wpm.description: words per minute of SPEAKING time — transcript words divided by the time spent producing them, not by the length of the recording. A speaker silent while their partner talks does not read as a slow one

echo_cancellation.description: whether echo cancellation was applied at capture, as reported by the client (a capture setting, not measured from audio); null where the client reported nothing

headphones.description: whether the speaker used headphones (authoritative on mobile, heuristic on web)

recording.description: { sample_rate (delivered Hz), original_sample_rate (verified native capture Hz), duration_seconds, bit_depth: 16, channels: 1, integrated_lufs (measured LUFS, nullable), true_peak_dbtp (measured dBTP, nullable), loudness_normalization (present only on a normalized archive) } — audio is delivered at its recorded level unless the archive was built with a loudness normalization setting; loudness + true-peak are measured on the rendition shipped here, after any normalization, rather than on any other, so you can normalize to your own target

conversation_after.description: the conversation level in the chosen measure after the change; null for per-track settings

conversation_before.description: the conversation level in the chosen measure before the change; null for per-track settings

gain_db.description: the volume change applied to this track, in dB

limited_by.description: "clipping" = the change stopped just below full scale, so the result is below the target; "unmeasurable" = nothing to measure, so the track is unchanged; null when the target was reached

measure.description: "lufs" = loudness (ITU-R BS.1770), "rms" = average level over the whole file including pauses, "peak" = the loudest sample

method.description: "constant_gain": one volume change for the whole track, with no compression or limiting

scope.description: "conversation" = one shared change for every speaker in the conversation; "track" = a separate change for each track

setting.description: the setting as scope:measure:target, e.g. conversation:rms:-20

target.description: the level the setting asks for, e.g. -20

target_reached.description: true when the result is within 0.1 dB of the target

track_after.description: { lufs, rms_dbfs, sample_peak_dbfs } of this track as delivered

track_before.description: { lufs, rms_dbfs, sample_peak_dbfs } of this track before the change

unit.description: "LUFS" for lufs, "dBFS" for rms and peak
